answer: Make penalties grow with correlation. A key that gives one bad verdict loses a small bond, but when many keys err the same way in the same epoch, each one's loss rises with the size of that crowd. A lone grader's slip, like one bruised apple in an orchard, costs little. A farm whose hundred keys run one script fails all at once, and that shared mistake is the signal that multiplies every slash. Like a terrace where all the stones slide together, the cluster pays far more than its parts would apart.
